body:
> **Review only the last commit, [`8546bde64e`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/commit/8546bde64e).** This PR builds on two open PRs, which are merged into its branch: hazelgrove/hazel#2661 (types get a Merkle hash) and hazelgrove/hazel#2679 (a push gives a value back when it already has the type). Once they land, merging `dev` into this branch shrinks the diff to that one commit.
>
> The two conflict with each other in `Ascriptions.re`: each adds a helper in the same spot. Merge commit `a032bd5c6a` keeps both, and whichever of them merges second needs the same resolution.

## What

Pushing an ascription through a value (`Ascriptions.transition_multiple`) walks all of it, making a temporary `Asc` node with a fresh id for every part, even when the value already has the type and comes back unchanged (#2679). A value is pushed through at every call of a function whose parameter is annotated (`fun x : T -> ...`). So:

- a value given to several such functions is walked again at each;
- a recursive one over a list is given the list's tail each time, so the walks over one list add up to the square of its length.

This PR remembers, by object identity, the data values that a push gave back unchanged, per type hash. Values are immutable, so the next push through one is a single lookup.

## The change

- **`has_type`**, in `Ascriptions`, maps a value to the type hashes it is known to have (`TypHash`, from #2661).
  - **Keys:** a value's term object, which a variable lookup keeps (`fast_copy` copies only the outer record). Lists are keyed by their OCaml cells, because a list's tail is a new `ListLit` around the same cells (`Unboxing`). Every tail of a list that has the type is remembered too.
  - **What's remembered:** only values with parts. An atom or a bare constructor is checked in one match, cheaper than a lookup.
  - **When:** only when a recursive push gave the value back unchanged. A value that needed a function wrapped, or that doesn't have the type, is never remembered.
- **`transition`** becomes a thin wrapper: for a recursive push, it checks `has_type` first and records afterwards. The existing body is unchanged, renamed `step`.
- **`Util.IdentityTable`** (new on `dev`, from the livelits branches): a table keyed by object identity, in a JS `WeakMap`, so an entry lives only as long as its value.

The context in `Ascriptions` is always `Ctx.empty`, as for `consistent_memo`, so whether a value has a type depends only on the value and the type's hash.

## Measured

Node, `dev`'s test build with #2661 and #2679. A recursive function over a list of n pairs, with the memo off and on interleaved in one process, medians of 5:

| function | n = 200 | n = 400 |
|---|---|---|
| `let len = fun ys : [(Int, Int)] -> ...` (annotated parameter) | 61 → 14 ms | 205 → 33 ms |
| `let len : [(Int, Int)] -> Int = fun ys -> ...` (annotated at the let) | 19 → 21 ms | 35 → 36 ms |

The first grows with the square of n without the memo. The second isn't pushed through on its recursive calls, so there's nothing to save, and the memo costs nothing measurable.

On the livelits branch (hazelgrove/hazel#2635, the same change), the Scenes slide's woods picture view in Firefox: 563.5 → 497.5 ms per figure move, the view's own evaluation, median of 20 per build, alternating builds. There the values are the picture's shapes, each given to several functions with annotated parameters.

## Tests

- `Ascriptions`, two new cases:
  - after one push, a list's tails are known to have its type, and only that type;
  - a value without the type is not remembered.
- The existing case with a list of functions now pushes twice and checks that the value is never remembered.
- Mutation-checked on #2635: remembering a changed value, or not remembering the tails, each fails a test.
- `Ascriptions` 4, `TypHash` 10, `Evaluator` 492, `Elaboration` 39, `Stepper` 20 and `Probe` 280 pass.

commits.messageBody:
TypHash: a hash of a type from its constructor and its children's hashes,
ids ignored, so copies of one type hash alike. Each type object's hash is
kept in a JS WeakMap keyed by the object, so asking again is one lookup
and a type built from parts already hashed costs only its new nodes. Two
independent 30-bit hashes make a key of about 60 bits. A type holding an
expression, a signature or projector data gets no hash, and callers then
compute as if there were no cache.

Ascriptions: a constructor application ascribed a sum type asks whether
the constructor's own sum type is consistent with it -- a full meet of
two copies of the same sum type, for every application it ascribes. The
answer is now cached by the two types' hashes (consistent_by_hash). The
context there is always Ctx.empty, and is_consistent ignores an Unknown's
provenance, as the hash does.

On dev, `hazel bench-eval` of a recursive builder of a 20-constructor
sum, 600 nodes: 74-75 ms before, 58-63 ms after (three runs each). On
the livelits branch, whose Html views are trees of such applications, a
click on the Polygons drawing editor went from 15-17 s to about 2 s in
Firefox.

Tests: TypHash (10). Evaluator, Elaboration, Unboxing and Coverage pass.
Issue #2609.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Types get a Merkle hash; the evaluator asks is_consistent once per pair

commits.messageBody:
…eady has the type

Pushing an ascription all the way through a value (transition_multiple)
rebuilt it, every list cell and tuple field, even when nothing inside
changed, in one evaluation step. A well-typed list crossing a typed
parameter was copied whole each time: time and garbage, and new objects
for anything that keeps values by identity.

The list, cons, tuple, label and constructor cases now build a new node
only when a part came back different, and otherwise give the value
itself: plain data that already has the type crosses a typed boundary as
the same objects, with its ids, as the file's header asks. A value
holding a function is still wrapped. The Parens case passes its value on
rather than a fresh copy of it, for the same reason.

hazel bench-eval, 15 runs each, A/B/A on one machine: a list of 2,000
labeled tuples passed 30 times through a typed parameter, plain
evaluation 269 / 382 (dev) / 267 ms; bench/eval-bench.hz 764 / 764
(dev) / 749 ms. On the livelits integration branch the same change took
the Scenes slide's picture view from about 725-830 to 520-650 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
